raw: 21.1 Information Warfare Doctrine: Definitions, Theory, Air Force Policy[^101][^102]
teaching_note: An Air Force-hosted policy study and a scholarly argument are different from adopted doctrine or current authorization. Identify author, date, genre and scope before comparing their definitions; distinguish public information duties, military information activities and the curriculum's analysis-only boundary [@ageint101; @ageint102].
title: Information warfare: historical policy arguments and theory

raw: 21.2 Military Deception: Six Principles and Historical Effectiveness[^103][^104]
teaching_note: A journal topic index and a practitioner essay do not establish a canonical six-principle doctrine or a general success rate. Frequency of reported deception is prevalence, not effectiveness; a selected successful case lacks the counterfactual and failed cases needed for a causal estimate. Study claims and source selection without reproducing deception planning [@ageint103; @ageint104].
title: Military deception: historical arguments and limits of effectiveness claims

raw: 21.3 Automated Influence and the Cognitive Security Challenge[^105]
teaching_note: The cited work proposes cognitive security as an ethical and analytic lens for automated influence, not an established detector or validated intervention stack. Preserve agency: disagreement and rhetorical style are not attacks or diagnoses, and a response should help learners examine evidence rather than engineer their beliefs [@ageint105].
title: Automated Influence and the Cognitive Security Challenge

raw: 21.4 Cognitive Security in the Age of AI: NATO/EU Paradigm Shift[^95]
teaching_note: A policy paper hosted on Academia does not establish NATO or EU adoption, consensus or measured efficacy. Any institutional position requires its own dated primary statement; keep the inherited 'paradigm shift' wording as source history, not a factual conclusion [@ageint095].
title: Cognitive Security in the Age of AI: an attributed policy proposal

raw: 21.5 Epistemic Chaos as an Adversarial Goal[^95][^96]
teaching_note: Confusion can result from error, incomplete evidence or ordinary disagreement as well as deliberate activity. A conceptual description of a possible objective does not establish a particular actor's motive, coordination or success; keep activity, intent, sponsor and impact as separate claims [@ageint095; @ageint096].
title: Epistemic Chaos as a hypothesized adversarial goal

raw: 21.6 Active Inference and Predictive Processing as Models for Cognitive Attack/Defense[^106][^3]
teaching_note: Active inference supplies a formal modeling vocabulary for beliefs, observations and action under explicit assumptions; a model fit does not uniquely identify a human mechanism or hostile influence. The undergraduate review and broader theoretical material do not validate a cognitive-attack detector, an individual cognitive score or a human/agent isomorphism. Compare model predictions with alternatives rather than diagnose real people [@ageint106; @ageint003].
title: Active Inference and Predictive Processing as Models for Cognitive Attack/Defense

raw: 21.7 Behavioral Outcomes of Human Cognitive Security (arXiv 2026)[^107]
teaching_note: The preprint proposes a construct and computational models, including a fit to empirical illusory-truth data; that grounding is not field-tested intervention assurance, and veracity judgment, sharing intention, observed sharing and task action remain distinct [@ageint107]. Completed offline case: synthetic source cards mark A/B true and C/D false; a supplied learner response accepts A/C and rejects B/D, so discernment is 2/4, while separate intended-sharing responses name A/B/C and no sharing is observed. Withheld card E corrects the source label for C to true: recomputation yields 3/4, not evidence that an intervention improved the learner, because the answer key changed. The filled conclusion is packet-specific classification only, with no causal effect, actor attribution or psychological diagnosis; stop at that boundary and preserve the correction (see [@sec:analytic-workflow]).
title: Behavioral Outcomes of Human Cognitive Security (arXiv 2026)
